about.title: Avenal Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Avenal is a small Kings County community of about 13,300 people, the kind of place where a single loss is felt on every block. Public records show the city closed out 2025 with two injury collisions and no traffic deaths, a quiet year on Route 269, Route 33, San Joaquin Street and Skyline Boulevard. Still, wrongful death claims reach far beyond the road. A fall at a worksite, a mistake in medical care, a defective piece of equipment, or a crash on a rural highway heading toward the coast can all leave a family without a parent, a partner, or a child. California law lets certain surviving relatives bring a civil claim to recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. That claim runs separately from any criminal case and carries its own deadline. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Avenal families with an independent attorney who can explain what applies to your situation, with no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Avenal Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing, starting with a spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out who in your family is eligible before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines that don't wait for grief
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity is involved. Getting connected early protects that timeline.

items.title: A full picture of what can be recovered
items.desc: Funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance are all recognized under California law. An independent attorney can help document each of these honestly.

items.question: Avenal had no traffic deaths in 2025. Do wrongful death cases still happen here?
items.answer: Yes. Traffic collisions are only one source of wrongful death claims, and even a year with no fatalities on Route 269 or Skyline Boulevard doesn't cover deaths from workplace accidents, unsafe property, medical negligence or defective products. Families in Avenal have the same rights under California law as anyone in a larger city. The size of the town doesn't change the claim.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as the criminal case against the person responsible?
items.answer: No, they are separate. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by the family to recover specific losses. A civil claim can move forward whether or not criminal charges are filed, and the outcome of one does not decide the other.

items.question: What if the death involved a county road or a state highway like Route 33?
items.answer: When a public agency may share responsibility, California requires a formal claim to that agency on a much shorter timeline than the standard two years, often a matter of months. Missing it can close the door on that part of the case. This is one reason it helps to speak with an attorney soon after a loss, even while you are still gathering information.
